title: Normality of the finite supremum from a normal-fiber cover
statement: Let A be a domain and K its fraction field. Let s be a finite set of A-subalgebras of K all contained in the integral closure of A in K. Suppose for every prime p of A, some C in s has integrally closed localizations at every prime of C contracting to p. Then every prime localization of the supremum S of s is integrally closed. No Noetherian hypothesis, local-approximation hypothesis, or finite-module hypothesis is needed for this algebraic step.

proof.text: Finset.sup_le gives S contained in the integral closure; hence its elements are integral over A. For q in Spec S, contract to p in Spec A and choose C in s by the covering hypothesis. The inclusion C -> S exists by Finset.le_sup. Its contraction r of q is prime, lies over p by functoriality of contraction, and C_r is integrally closed by the hypothesis.

A lies in C inside K, so K is the fraction field of C and of C_r. Every element of S is integral over A and thus over C_r. Localizing S at C minus r yields an integral extension T of C_r embedded in K, since the denominators are units of C_r. Every element of T is integral over C_r, hence normality of C_r identifies T with C_r inside K. This is the defining property isIntegrallyClosed_iff, together with integrality of sums and products and localization universal properties.
C minus r maps into S minus q. Thus S_q is a further localization of T = C_r, at nonzero denominators. Normality of localizations gives IsIntegrallyClosed S_q.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_normal_cover_sup_normal (A : Type u) (K : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (s : Finset (Subalgebra A K))
    (hs : ∀ C ∈ s, C ≤ integralClosure A K)
    (hcover : ∀ (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime], ∃ C ∈ s,
      ∀ (q : Ideal C) [q.IsPrime], Ideal.comap (algebraMap A C) q = p →
        IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime q)) :
    ∀ (q : Ideal (s.sup (fun C : Subalgebra A K => C) : Subalgebra A K)) [q.IsPrime],
      IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime q)
